boards.name: BeaglePlay
boards.summary: No DIP switches: remove SD and leave USR released.
steps: Disconnect power and remove the recovery SD card.
Leave the USR button released (do not press it).
Reconnect power to start the installed eMMC image.
notes: USR is beside the microSD slot. BeaglePlay has fixed boot straps, so there is no filesystem-mode DIP setting.
TOBI recovery installations prepare a verified first-stage loader in eMMC Boot0. The remaining stages load from the user-area filesystem.
Third-party images require their own compatible eMMC bootloader layout. A completed disk write alone does not prepare that layout.

sources.title: AM69 Processor Starter Kit Evaluation Module, SPRUJ70B
TI expert correction: SK-AM69 does not support eMMC UDA boot
Official AM69 SK hardware setup and switch photograph
Table2-3: boot settings
TI AM69-SK: hardware boot partition programming and ROM configuration

notes: SPRUJ70B Table2-3 lists eMMC OFF/ON/ON and also repeats that pattern as Reserved, a table defect. TI support confirms UDA boot unsupported after correcting confusion with the full AM69 EVM. No full-EVM SW8/SW9 or SW11/SW7 settings apply to SK-AM69.
This starter kit cannot select ROM filesystem boot from the eMMC user area with its stock switches. The setting above selects hardware eMMC boot and requires a prepared Boot0 loader.
TOBI recovery installations must prepare a verified first-stage loader in Boot0 before reporting success. The patched SPL then reads the remaining stages from the user-area filesystem.
Third-party images need a compatible eMMC bootloader layout. If boot preparation fails, retain SD boot instead of trying an incomplete installation.
Automatic SK-AM69 Boot0 preparation requires a TOBI build containing this board-guide change. The previously published 2026.10.2 image does not include that fix; keep SD boot until updated.
recovery_steps: Disconnect power and reinsert the TOBI recovery SD card.
For SD boot, set SW2 switches 1, 2 and 3 OFF; leave switch 4 unchanged.
Reconnect power and correct any image or Boot0 preparation error before retrying.
